title: Treasure Island
tagline: Find the treasure. Try not to get eaten.
description: A fork in the road, a castle with suspicious doors, a lake full of very patient crocodiles, and a treasure that is exactly as valuable as you deserve.

fork.text:
Welcome to Treasure Island. Your mission is to find the treasure.

You arrive at a fork in the road. To the left, the spires of a crooked castle. To the right, the sound of rushing water. Behind you, your perfectly good boat.

end_sensible.text:
You decide treasure hunting on an island named after a pirate novel is a liability nightmare. You sail home, max out your retirement contributions, and live a long, quiet, deeply responsible life.

Somewhere, a narrator sighs.

cliff.text: The path ends at a cliff. A rusty zipline stretches down to a small island in a lake far below. A rickety ladder runs down the cliff face to the water's edge.

choices.label: Lash yourself to the zipline with the rope, then ride it

cliff_search.text:
Behind a bush you find a coil of sturdy rope and a laminated sign: ZIPLINE INSPECTED 1987.

You take the rope. You also take the hint.

end_zipline.text: Halfway down you hear a loud *crack*. The zipline, last inspected during the Reagan administration, gives up. You fall into the lake, where a crocodile who has been waiting a very long time for this exact moment eats you.

zipline_rope.text: The line snaps halfway down, exactly as you expected. Your rope catches the cable stump and you swing like a pendulum of pure competence, landing on the island's beach with only minor dignity loss.

lake.text:
At the bottom of the ladder the lake laps at your boots. The island is maybe a hundred yards out. Several logs float nearby.

One of the logs blinks.

end_swim.text: The logs were crocodiles. You knew the logs were crocodiles. The logs knew you knew. Nobody is surprised by how this goes.

shoreline.text: Around a bend you find an old rowboat with one oar and a hand-painted name on the side: S.S. PROBABLY FINE.

rowing.text: Halfway across, the crocodiles notice. Three of them start circling. The S.S. Probably Fine has a slow leak. Of course it does.

choices.label: Row like your life depends on it
Smack the nearest crocodile with the oar

end_oar.text: You bonk the crocodile on the nose. It's offended. Its friends are also offended. The S.S. Probably Fine turns out to be, ultimately, not.

island.text:
The island is tiny: one palm tree, one hut, and one extremely old man in a hammock who has clearly not had a visitor in decades.

"Riddle," he croaks, before you can say anything. "Answer it and I'll give you my map."

choices.label: Ignore him and climb the palm tree for coconuts
Ignore him and look behind the hut

riddle.text: "What," he says, with enormous gravity, "has keys, but can't open locks?"

choices.label: The guy who keeps losing his car keys

riddle_right.text:
He squints at you. "Correct. Nobody ever gets that one."

Everybody gets that one.

He hands you a yellowed map. A dotted line runs from the hut, under the lake, to a castle, ending at a big red X. In the margin: DON'T DRINK FROM THE CHALICE. NOT THE GOOD SPRITE.

choices.label: Thank him and look behind the hut

riddle_wrong.text: "Wrong," he says, and goes back to sleep. Deeply, unrecoverably asleep. You poke him. He snores louder. The map is clearly not happening.

choices.label: Climb the palm tree for coconuts

end_coconut.text: You climb thirty feet up a palm tree with no plan for coming down. You do eventually come down. All at once.

hut_back.text: Behind the hut, under a pile of old fishing nets, is a trapdoor. Below it, a damp tunnel heads under the lake toward the castle.

tunnel.text: The tunnel is long, dark, and smells like a gym bag left in a hot car. It ends at a ladder. You climb, push up a heavy flagstone, and haul yourself into...

castle_gate.text: You arrive at a mysterious castle. In the courtyard are three doors: one red, one yellow, and one gold.

end_red.text: You open the red door and immediately fall into a pit of small, slithery, extremely enthusiastic snakes. So sorry. You died.

yellow_room.text:
A dim room. A hunched figure in the corner turns around: a four-foot-eleven man in a stained bathrobe, eating a raw onion like an apple.

"I'm Gary. Night manager. You're gonna settle something for me." He leans in. "Is a hot dog a sandwich?"

end_gary.text: "WRONG," Gary screams, and beats you to death with a rolled-up newspaper from 1994. It takes a very long time. Neither of you enjoys it.

gary_friend.text:
"FINALLY," Gary says, wiping away a tear. "Somebody with sense."

He gives you a firm handshake and a business card that just says GARY. "You ever get in trouble in this castle, I got your back."

yellow_again.text: Gary salutes you with the onion. "Go get 'em, champ."

hallways.text: Behind the gold door the hallway splits: one passage goes forward, one to the left.

scratching_door.text: You find a door. From the other side: scratching, grunting, and what sounds like a man delivering an extremely intense monologue to an audience of no one.

end_bear.text:
In a wrestling ring, a man with alarming hair and a leather jacket is grappling with a grizzly bear. He locks eyes with you, whispers something in what might be Latin, and the bear immediately switches opponents.

You are mauled. He takes a bow.

turn_around.text:
You back away. Through the door a voice bellows: "COWARD!" Then, more quietly: "Honestly, good call."

You head the other way.

chalice.text: You enter a small room. On a pedestal sits a gold chalice full of a fizzing, ice-cold liquid. Condensation beads on the rim. It looks incredibly refreshing.

end_chalice.text:
Did no one ever tell you not to drink strange liquids you find in castles? Come on. You get dizzy. Your legs stop working. A short man in a bathrobe finds you, shakes his head, and feeds you to a pack of chihuahuas.

It's a lot of chihuahuas.

gary_rescue.text:
You get dizzy and collapse. When you wake up, Gary is fanning you with a newspaper. "Told you I had your back."

You never find the treasure. But Gary teaches you cribbage, you move into the yellow room, and it's honestly a pretty good life.

are_you_sure.text: ARE YOU SURE?! It looks SO refreshing. It might be the good gas-station Sprite. The one that burns a little.

end_peer.text: It was not the good gas-station Sprite. You have made a terrible mistake. You lose consciousness and never wake up. Honestly, your fault for caving to peer pressure from a narrator.

treasure_room.text:
A vaulted chamber. On a velvet pillow, under a single dramatic spotlight, is the treasure:

The keys to a 1990 Honda Civic, and a coupon for a free 20-piece chicken nugget meal. Expired.

choices.label: Line up the map and find the X
Pry up the suspiciously loose floor tile

end_civic.text:
Congrats. You win. I think?

The Civic has 340,000 miles on it and a tape deck permanently stuck on one song. You drive it home anyway. Legend.

end_true.text:
You count flagstones from the pedestal and pry up the one under the X. Beneath it: a chest of gold doubloons, a jeweled cutlass, and a note.

"The Civic was a decoy. -- Mgmt."

You are rich. You take the Civic anyway.

end_tile.text: The tile was loose because it's a trap. Obviously. The floor opens beneath you, and the last thing you see is the nugget coupon fluttering down after you like a tiny, greasy angel.
